name: John D. Rockefeller
fate_summary: Peak c.1913-1918 (~$0.9-1.2B). Gave ~$530M to philanthropy (Rockefeller Foundation, Univ. of Chicago, GEB, RIMR); transferred most of the rest (Standard Oil successor stock) to his son John D. Rockefeller Jr. 1917-1922 (on list) and some to daughters; probated estate only $26.4M in 1937.

name: John D. Rockefeller Jr.
fate_summary: Received the bulk of his father's fortune 1917-1922. Gave ~$537M to charity (Rockefeller Center-era, Colonial Williamsburg, parks, Riverside Church, RBF) and ~$240M to his own family (1934 and 1952 trusts for his children - Nelson, David, Laurance, JDR 3rd, Winthrop, Abby all on Fortune 1957 list); final disposition in 1950s: $73M to charity, $57M to Rockefeller Brothers Fund.

name: William Rockefeller
fate_summary: Standard Oil co-founder. Gross estate $102M in 1922, cut to ~$50M net by ~$30M debts and $18.6M estate/inheritance taxes; passed to children and a trust for great-grandchildren.

name: Henry Flagler
fate_summary: Standard Oil co-founder; spent ~$50M building the Florida East Coast Railway and hotels. Estate ($75M per 1917 transfer-tax report) went mainly to widow Mary Lily Kenan Flagler (d.1917), whose heirs were niece Louise Wise Lewis (Forbes 1918: $50M) and the Kenan family.

name: Anna M. Harkness
fate_summary: Widow of Stephen V. Harkness (d.1888; Standard Oil silent partner). Inherited ~1/3 of his fortune (~$50M), grew it to $85M while giving away ~$40M+; founded the Commonwealth Fund (1918, $10M). Estate went largely to son Edward S. Harkness (on list) and charity.

name: Charles W. Harkness
fate_summary: Son of Stephen V. Harkness; managed family Standard Oil holdings. No children; left half his fortune to brother Edward S. Harkness.

name: Lamon V. Harkness
fate_summary: Elder son of Stephen V. Harkness; estate passed to his children; contested residence/tax case in NY (1917).

name: Edward S. Harkness
fate_summary: Inherited from father Stephen, brother Charles (~$85M, 1916) and mother Anna (1926). Gave >$129M (with Commonwealth Fund): Harvard houses, Yale colleges, Columbia medical center, St Andrews. No children.

name: Oliver H. Payne
fate_summary: Standard Oil treasurer, bachelor. Passed most of his fortune to nephews before/at death: ~$63M to Payne Whitney, ~$12M to Harry Payne Whitney. Probated estate only ~$32M.

name: Payne Whitney
fate_summary: Heir of W.C. Whitney and uncle Oliver H. Payne. His 1927 estate was called the largest ever appraised in the US. >$20M to the Payne Whitney psychiatric clinic/NY Hospital; rest to widow Helen Hay Whitney and children John Hay "Jock" Whitney and Joan Whitney Payson (both on Fortune 1957 list, $100-200M).

name: Henry H. Rogers
fate_summary: Standard Oil executive; Virginian Railway. Fortune to children (incl. H.H. Rogers Jr., Mai Rogers Coe).

name: Edward L. Doheny
fate_summary: California/Mexico oil; Teapot Dome. Fortune to family (son Ned d.1929) and Catholic charities; not researched in detail.

name: Andrew Carnegie
fate_summary: Sold Carnegie Steel to J.P. Morgan (U.S. Steel) in 1901, personal share ~$226M in bonds; gave away $350.7M by 1919 (Carnegie Corporation of NY $125M, libraries $60M, CFAT $29M, Carnegie Institute & Institution $22M each, peace, hero funds, UK trusts). Remaining ~$30M estate to Carnegie Corporation (residuary), charities and pensions. Forbes 1918 ($200M) badly overstated him.

name: Henry Clay Frick
fate_summary: Carnegie partner; U.S. Steel/railroad investor. At death left ~$117M (five-sixths) to public purposes - the Frick Collection (house + art est. $50M), Princeton, Harvard, MIT, Frick Park - and ~$25M to family (daughter Helen Clay Frick, son Childs Frick).

name: Henry Phipps Jr.
fate_summary: Carnegie Steel's second-largest partner. Distributed fortune to children during life (e.g. $3M Chicago realty 1912); estate only $3.1M. Daughter Amy Phipps Guest on Fortune 1957 list ($200-400M); Phipps family on Forbes 400 1982.

name: Charles M. Schwab
fate_summary: Bethlehem Steel. Spent/lost his fortune (est. $25-40M before 1929); died insolvent, >$300K in debt.

name: J. P. Morgan
fate_summary: Estate $68.3M (c.$30M in his bank partnerships) - much smaller than assumed. Son J.P. Morgan Jr. inherited the firm and ~$50M; much of the art collection went to the Metropolitan Museum and Morgan Library.

name: J. P. Morgan Jr.
fate_summary: Grew inheritance via WWI Allied purchasing commissions; fortune later divided among children; not researched in detail.

name: George F. Baker
fate_summary: First National Bank of NY. Described at death (1931) as 3rd or 4th richest American. Gave $5M+ to found Harvard Business School campus. Fortune to son George F. Baker Jr. (d.1937; estate reported $50-100M).

name: James Stillman
fate_summary: National City Bank chairman, Rockefeller ally; fortune to children (James A. Stillman, Isabel & Elsie m. Rockefellers).

name: Russell Sage
fate_summary: Left his entire fortune (~$63-70M) to widow Olivia Sage, who gave most of it away.

name: Olivia Sage
fate_summary: Gave the Sage fortune away: Russell Sage Foundation ($10M, 1907), RPI, Yale ($650K), Cornell, Syracuse, Emma Willard; further bequests at death 1918.

name: Hetty Green
fate_summary: "Richest woman in America". Estate ($100M, est. range $100-200M) went to son E.H.R. "Ned" Green and daughter Sylvia Wilks; Sylvia left ~$200M to 64 charities on her death in 1951.

name: E. H. R. Green
fate_summary: Hetty Green's son; spent lavishly (yachts, stamps, coins). Estate ~$44.4M fought over by four states for ~$6M tax; passed to sister Sylvia.

name: E. H. Harriman
fate_summary: Union Pacific/Southern Pacific. Left everything to widow Mary W. Harriman in a dozen-word will; she gave Harriman State Park and endowed causes; sons W. Averell and E. Roland Harriman (Brown Brothers Harriman).

name: Mary W. Harriman
fate_summary: Managed the Harriman fortune; Harriman State Park (10,000 acres + $1M, 1910); eugenics funding; fortune to sons Averell and Roland.

name: Thomas Fortune Ryan
fate_summary: Wall Street speculator (traction, American Tobacco, Belgian Congo). Estate to children and grandchildren, much in trust.

name: Anthony N. Brady
fate_summary: Traction and utility promoter; fortune to sons Nicholas F. Brady (Forbes 1918: $60M) and James C. Brady.

name: Cornelius Vanderbilt II
fate_summary: Died Sep 1899 (just before window). Estate $73M: ~$42M to son Alfred G. Vanderbilt (who gave $6M to disinherited brother Cornelius III), $20M trust for four younger children, $9M to widow Alice.

name: Alfred G. Vanderbilt
fate_summary: Principal heir of Cornelius II; died on the Lusitania. NY estate ~$16.8M + $4.6M trust (1917 appraisal) to widow and sons.

name: William K. Vanderbilt
fate_summary: Inherited $55M (1885). Settled >$17M on daughter Consuelo (Duchess of Marlborough) over his life. Gross estate $54.5M; ~$13.4M federal+NY estate tax; residue to sons W.K. Vanderbilt II and Harold S. Vanderbilt.

name: Frederick W. Vanderbilt
fate_summary: Childless; estate ($79.8M gross/$72.8M net) mostly to wife's niece Margaret Van Alen and relatives; $5.2M to Yale Sheffield Scientific School; Hyde Park mansion to the nation.

name: George W. Vanderbilt II
fate_summary: Builder of Biltmore; spent much of his inheritance. Widow and daughter Cornelia inherited; Pisgah forest sold to the US.

name: George J. Gould
fate_summary: Eldest son of Jay Gould; inherited $15M (1892) and ran the Gould rail system, which largely collapsed by 1918. Estate $15.05M gross, $5.18M after settling suits.

name: James J. Hill
fate_summary: Great Northern Railway. Widow received >$16M, each child ~$4M; $1.5M income & inheritance taxes.

name: Collis P. Huntington
fate_summary: Central/Southern Pacific. Estate split between widow Arabella, nephew Henry E. Huntington (one-third) and stepson Archer; art (c.$3M) to the Met.

name: Henry E. Huntington
fate_summary: Los Angeles streetcars and land; married uncle's widow Arabella (1913). Fortune largely to the Huntington Library, Art Museum and Botanical Gardens.

name: William C. Whitney
fate_summary: Navy Secretary turned traction financier; sons Harry Payne Whitney (inherited $24M) and Payne Whitney.

name: Peter A. B. Widener
fate_summary: Philadelphia streetcars; huge art collection (Lynnewood Hall) later given by son Joseph to the National Gallery (1942).

name: John Jacob Astor IV
fate_summary: Died on the Titanic. $69M of his $87M estate to son Vincent Astor; $5M trust + $100K to widow Madeleine; $3M trust for posthumous son John Jacob VI.

name: Vincent Astor
fate_summary: Created the Vincent Astor Foundation (1948, $60.5M); estate (~$127M) largely to the foundation, run by widow Brooke Astor, which gave away ~$175M and closed in 1997.

name: William Waldorf Astor
fate_summary: Moved to England 1891; transferred much to sons Waldorf and John Jacob V before death. No reliable total found; only NYC real estate (~$60M) at death.

name: Marshall Field
fate_summary: Estate ($125M; papers reported up to $150M) mostly in trust for grandsons Marshall Field III and Henry Field until age 50; $8M to the Field Museum.

name: Julius Rosenwald
fate_summary: Sears president; gave ~$63M+ (Rosenwald schools, Museum of Science and Industry); pledged $21M of his own wealth to rescue Sears in the slump.

name: Sam Walton
fate_summary: Richest American 1985-1988 (Forbes). Shares held via Walton Enterprises partnership already split with his four children; family fortune intact after his 1992 death.

name: William A. Clark
fate_summary: Montana copper king and US senator. Fortune divided among five children incl. Huguette Clark (d.2011); art bequeathed to the Corcoran Gallery.

name: Frederick Weyerhaeuser
fate_summary: Timber syndicate leader; wealth held as shares in many family lumber companies, passed to children (John P., Frederick E., Rudolph, Charles). Size of fortune is highly uncertain.

name: Daniel Guggenheim
fate_summary: Head of the Guggenheim brothers (family fortune est. $250-300M in 1918); individual share below threshold.

name: Calouste Gulbenkian
fate_summary: Bulk of fortune and art collection to the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, Lisbon (1956); undisclosed trusts for descendants.

name: J. Ogden Armour
fate_summary: Armour & Co. lost $125M in 1919-21; Armour lost most of a ~$100M+ stock fortune and died with <$25K cash plus ~$3M of then-illiquid UOP stock.

name: Philip D. Armour
fate_summary: Founder of Armour & Co.; fortune to son J. Ogden Armour and Armour Institute.

name: John T. Dorrance
fate_summary: Sole owner of Campbell Soup; estate to children incl. John T. Dorrance Jr. (Fortune 1957: $75-100M).

name: William Weightman
fate_summary: Philadelphia chemical maker and landlord; fortune passed to daughter Anne Weightman Walker Penfield (not researched further).

name: Claus Spreckels
fate_summary: Sugar refining; fortune to sons (litigated). Not researched further.

name: Adolphus Busch
fate_summary: Anheuser-Busch; fortune to widow and children (August A. Busch). K&G list gives death year as 1919 in error.

name: Charles L. Tiffany
fate_summary: Tiffany & Co.; fortune to children incl. Louis Comfort Tiffany.

name: John W. Mackay
fate_summary: Comstock silver; Postal Telegraph; fortune to son Clarence Mackay.

name: James B. Duke
fate_summary: American Tobacco, Duke Power. Created the Duke Endowment (1924) and left it about half his ~$100M estate (another $67M); rest to daughter Doris Duke and widow Nanaline.

name: Doris Duke
fate_summary: Inherited most of J.B. Duke's private fortune (in stages) and $250M from her mother (1962). Left ~$1.2B (1993) mostly to the Doris Duke Charitable Foundation.

name: Henry Ford
fate_summary: Bought out minority holders 1919, so the Ford family owned all of Ford Motor. To escape 1935 estate taxes he and Edsel left the non-voting Class A stock (~95% of equity) to the Ford Foundation (est. 1936) and voting Class B to grandchildren (Henry Ford II, Benson, William Clay, Josephine).

name: Edsel Ford
fate_summary: Held ~42% of Ford Motor. At his death Time estimated a 75% tax of ~$225M on his holdings, so they went (as non-voting stock) to the Ford Foundation; voting stock to his children.

name: Horace E. Dodge
fate_summary: Died 1920 months after brother John; widows sold Dodge Brothers to Dillon, Read in 1925; fortune to widow Anna Thompson Dodge and children.

name: John F. Dodge
fate_summary: Fortune to widow Matilda Dodge Wilson (later founded Oakland University) and children.

name: Pierre S. du Pont
fate_summary: Led DuPont and General Motors; Longwood Gardens; fortune to Longwood Foundation (no children). No sourced figure after 1918.

name: Alfred I. du Pont
fate_summary: Estate $56M, of which $30M paid in estate tax; rest in trust for widow Jessie Ball duPont, becoming the Alfred I. duPont Testamentary Trust / Nemours Foundation ($72.5M 1939, $2B 1981).

name: Andrew W. Mellon
fate_summary: Treasury Secretary 1921-32. Gave his art collection (est. $19M+) and ~$9-10M for the building to found the National Gallery of Art; much of fortune moved to the A.W. Mellon Educational & Charitable Trust and to children Paul Mellon and Ailsa Mellon Bruce (both on Fortune 1957 list).

name: Richard B. Mellon
fate_summary: Andrew's brother and partner. Fortune reported at $200M though will filed disposed of only $2M (rest pre-transferred); $13.3M estate tax. Heirs: Richard King Mellon and Sarah Mellon Scaife.

name: Paul Mellon
fate_summary: Andrew's son; huge gifts to National Gallery, Yale Center for British Art; Old Dominion Foundation merged into the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation (1969).

name: Ailsa Mellon Bruce
fate_summary: Andrew's daughter; Avalon Foundation (merged into Andrew W. Mellon Foundation 1969); co-funded NGA East Wing; left bulk of estate to charity and 153 paintings to the NGA.

name: Richard King Mellon
fate_summary: R.B.'s son; ran Mellon Bank; Richard King Mellon Foundation; Fortune 1968: his four children each reputed to have $100M+.

name: Sarah Mellon Scaife
fate_summary: R.B.'s daughter; Sarah Scaife Foundation; children Richard Mellon Scaife and Cordelia Scaife May on Fortune 1968 list.

name: Arthur Vining Davis
fate_summary: No children; $400M estate largely to the Arthur Vining Davis Foundations.

name: Cyrus H. K. Curtis
fate_summary: Curtis Publishing (Saturday Evening Post, Ladies Home Journal); fortune much reduced in the Depression; heir daughter Mary Louise Curtis Bok.

name: George Eastman
fate_summary: Bachelor; gave ~$100M (Rochester, MIT, Eastman School, dental clinics); residue to University of Rochester.

name: Robert Wood Johnson II
fate_summary: Left the bulk of his ~$400M estate (J&J stock) to the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation.

name: J. Paul Getty
fate_summary: Richest American by Fortune 1957 and 1968. At death left Getty Oil stock worth ~$660-700M to the J. Paul Getty Museum (worth $1.2B when released in 1982); family wealth sat in the Sarah C. Getty Trust (son Gordon Getty trustee), which received $4.1B when Texaco bought Getty Oil in 1984.

name: Gordon Getty
fate_summary: Sole trustee of the Sarah C. Getty Trust; sold Getty Oil to Texaco (1984) for ~$10B, trust receiving $4.1B; trust later split among family branches (1985).

name: Howard Hughes
fate_summary: Inherited Hughes Tool (1924). Gave Hughes Aircraft to the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (1953; sold to GM for $5.2B in 1985). Sold TWA stake for $546M (1966) and bought Las Vegas hotels. Died intestate (Mormon Will rejected); estate (~$2.3-2.5B est.) split in 1983 among 22 cousins incl. William Lummis.

name: H. L. Hunt
fate_summary: East Texas oil. Set up trusts (Placid Oil etc.) reputedly worth >$100M each for his six first-family children (Fortune 1968); sons Nelson Bunker, W. Herbert, Lamar, Ray Lee Hunt.

name: Nelson Bunker Hunt
fate_summary: Libyan Sarir oil fortune (nationalised 1973). With brother W. Herbert tried to corner silver 1979-80; Silver Thursday collapse; Chapter 11 in 1988.

name: W. Herbert Hunt
fate_summary: Partner in the 1979-80 silver corner; bankruptcy 1988; still on Forbes 400 decades later.

name: Daniel K. Ludwig
fate_summary: Lost ~ $1B on the Jari pulp project in Brazil (sold 1981-82). No heirs; fortune to the Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research (endowment ~$700M by 1992) and Ludwig cancer centers.

name: Sid W. Richardson
fate_summary: Bachelor; fortune to nephew Perry R. Bass (whose sons Sid, Ed, Robert, Lee Bass became billionaires) and the Sid W. Richardson Foundation.

name: Sid R. Bass
fate_summary: Grand-nephew of Sid Richardson; Bass brothers investing (Disney, Texaco stakes).

name: Clint Murchison Sr.
fate_summary: Fortune passed to sons Clint Jr. (Dallas Cowboys; bankrupt 1985) and John D. Murchison.

name: Joseph P. Kennedy
fate_summary: Set up $1M+ trusts for each of nine children; fortune spread across Kennedy heirs, none individually near the top.

name: John D. MacArthur
fate_summary: One of the few US billionaires in the 1970s; left ~92% of estate to the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.

name: Edwin H. Land
fate_summary: Polaroid founder; holdings fell sharply with the stock after 1968; Rowland Institute.

name: David Packard
fate_summary: Left ~ $4B (bulk of estate) to the David and Lucile Packard Foundation (1996).

name: H. Ross Perot
fate_summary: Sold EDS to General Motors (1984).

name: John Kluge
fate_summary: Took Metromedia private (1984) and sold TV stations (1985-86); richest American 1989-90.

name: Warren Buffett
fate_summary: Still alive; pledged most of fortune to Gates Foundation and family foundations (2006 onward).

name: Forrest Mars Sr.
fate_summary: Private company passed intact to children (John, Forrest Jr., Jacqueline).

name: David Rockefeller
fate_summary: Youngest son of JDR Jr.; the only Rockefeller in the Forbes billionaire class by 1986.

name: Sir John Ellerman, 1st Baronet
fate_summary: Richest man in Britain; estate sworn (1936) at GBP 36,684,994 excl. foreign property, the largest British estate to that date; passed to son Sir John Ellerman, 2nd Bt (heavy death duties).

name: Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach
fate_summary: Sole owner of Krupp; convicted at Nuremberg, fortune restored 1951. Shortly before his death the firm was converted to a corporation owned by the Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach Foundation; son Arndt renounced the inheritance for an annuity.
